children: Kalshi traders are pricing a significant chance that the U.S. will enact an AI "kill switch" law amid growing warnings from researchers that increasingly capable AI systems could pose an existential threat to humanity.

Earlier in the month, Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger said he personally believed there was a greater than 10% chance AI could “kill all humans” within the next decade. He also said Anthropic
did not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and was not clearly on track to do so.
Kalshi's market showed a 57% chance of the U.S. enacting an AI kill-switch law before Jan. 1, 2028. The odds were 33% for legislation before July 1, 2027, and 7% before Jan. 1, 2027.

The market comes as lawmakers consider whether existing safeguards are sufficient to address catastrophic AI risks. Senators Ted Cruz, Amy Klobuchar, and John Thune are working on bipartisan AI safety legislation that would create legal duties for AI companies to manage catastrophic risks, according to Semafor. The proposal remained under negotiation.

Among the ideas discussed is a legal “duty of care” requiring AI developers to take steps to protect against major risks from their systems, Reuters reported. The proposed framework is broader than a literal kill switch and would address how developers assess and mitigate potentially catastrophic risks.
The legislative discussions follow calls from AI executives and researchers for greater caution around the development of advanced systems. OpenAI
has called for independent groups to conduct more extensive testing of AI models and investigate serious incidents involving AI systems.

as an embedded evaluator for AI safety work after CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower pace of AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk have also backed greater caution around advanced AI systems.
